compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
Plan review and code review currently make discovery decisions through partially independent registry, routing, runner, checkpoint, and failure paths. This lets one review schedule disabled built-ins, omit activated project DET criteria, ignore project applicability or an authored budget, and mistake failed work for a successful checkpoint. The recovered RP-06 design and the completed research on `rubellite-secondary-cub` establish that these are policy-ownership defects, not merely duplicated code.

The durable intent sources are session log `supporting-chummy-snake`, recovery ticket `irascible-clueless-basenji`, and the approved decisions recorded on `rubellite-secondary-cub`. RP-01 remains authoritative for request-local provider retry, context, output-size, and structured-output behavior; this epic does not create another provider retry loop or truncate authoritative review input.

## Outcome and Architecture
Implement one review-discovery architecture:

`CriteriaSnapshot -> gate-owned strategy -> DiscoveryStagePlan -> shared executor -> DiscoveryStageResult -> gate-owned verdict policy`

One immutable repository-bound effective-policy snapshot includes built-ins, project LLM criteria, project DET criteria, routing, prompts, posture, applicability, and a digest. Gate strategies retain their own context and topology rules. The shared executor owns typed unit outcomes, usage, budget enforcement, cancellation, and success-only checkpoint mechanics; it does not choose applicability, truncate inputs, retry provider turns, or decide a gate verdict.

The final failure policy continues independent work after RP-01 exhausts a local operation, retains successful findings, skips dependency-blocked work with provenance, and returns unsigned `INDETERMINATE` when blocking-capable coverage is missing unless a real blocking finding takes precedence. Advisory-only gaps may still pass. Systemic configuration, cancellation, deterministic-floor, and whole-tier failure behavior remains fail-safe.

## Required Behavior
- Project code-review LLM criteria require a non-empty list of non-empty repository-relative globs; `["**"]` means repository-wide. Migrate `project.review-phase-boundaries` from `[]` to `["**"]` without changing its current membership.
- Built-in criteria retain their established secondary-trigger semantics, project DET remains detector-selected, and plan-review project criteria retain `applies_at` and `trigger` semantics.
- Positive explicit `usd_budget` values are authoritative. Omission is uncapped for code review; zero remains invalid and never acts as a disable switch.
- Preserve code review sequential execution, no code-review checkpoints, base-reviewer payloads, one-hop Round B, and authored YAML/BPMN topology.
- Preserve plan review chunking, concurrency, cache warming, checkpointing, container/prerequisite stages, and cancellation behavior while moving to a new digest-complete success-only checkpoint namespace. Legacy checkpoints never seed the new path.
- Persist a versioned typed discovery trace for retry, audit, and diagnostics. Review and review-status responses remain narrow end-result contracts and do not expose per-unit debugging detail, raw prompts, ticket content, provider payloads, or secrets.
- Add `rebar review-plan --retry`: only the literal latest completed `INDETERMINATE` review with retryable missing calls is eligible; reuse content-identical successes, retry only missing calls, and grant each explicit retry a fresh attempt budget. Changed or unreadable lineage refuses with zero calls. `--retry` is incompatible with `--force`, `--status`, and `--check`, while `--no-sign` remains compatible.
- Document `--retry` in canonical CLI help, generated command reference, the user guide, the plan-review gate guide, and exit-code guidance.
- The workflow editor shows editable Authored Workflow separately from read-only Effective Policy.

## Migration and Rollback
Use expand-contract without duplicate model calls: compute the legacy and new deterministic projections from the same observed calls, compare selection/order/context/model/budget/posture/usage/checkpoint decisions, and allow only approved deltas. Keep the legacy projection non-default during the compatibility window so a code revert can restore it; do not add an operator configuration flag solely for rollback. New code ignores legacy checkpoint envelopes, and old code ignores the new namespace.

## Testing
Each child begins with the smallest RED oracle that crosses its real seam: in-process policy and executor tests, real producer-to-consumer contract tests for journals and verdicts, real CLI subprocess tests for `--retry`, workflow-editor tests for authored/effective separation, and a final live review exercise because this epic cuts over production LLM paths. Stateful fault tests assert exact partial results, collateral state, and clean retry behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Both review gates derive selection from one immutable effective-policy snapshot, including effective built-in retunes/disables and activated project LLM/DET criteria.
- [ ] The shared discovery executor emits typed success, resumed, skipped, shed, failed, and cancelled outcomes; only success/resumed outcomes can seed the new checkpoint namespace.
- [ ] Code review preserves its scheduler, base-reviewer, topology, and narrow response contracts while enforcing approved applicability, budget, and partial-failure behavior.
- [ ] Plan review preserves its scheduler, cache, topology, and narrow response contracts while using digest-complete journals and approved partial-failure behavior.
- [ ] `rebar review-plan --retry` reuses eligible successes, retries only missing work with a fresh budget, refuses all stale/ineligible lineages before any model call, and is documented on every canonical operator surface.
- [ ] The workflow editor separates editable Authored Workflow from read-only Effective Policy and rejects an empty project code-review LLM glob list with the `["**"]` remedy.
- [ ] Cross-gate shadow traces show only approved behavior deltas, and a live end-to-end exercise proves the defaulted discovery paths against a real supported provider before the epic closes.
